recipes.name: Spinach and Strawberry Salad
ingredients_raw: 2 bunches spinach, rinsed and torn into bite-size pieces

steps.text: Toss spinach and strawberries together in a large bowl.
Whisk oil, sugar, vinegar, sesame seeds, poppy seeds, and paprika together in a medium bowl; pour over spinach and strawberries, and toss to coat.

raw_recipe.headline: Spinach and Strawberry Salad
raw_recipe.description: This easy spinach strawberry salad is packed with greens, fresh strawberries, and a deliciously sweet sesame and poppy seed vinaigrette dressing.

video.description: Make a top-rated salad with fresh spinach and fresh strawberries. These two power foods just happen to taste amazing together, and the popp-seed dressing is the perfect touch.

review.reviewBody: This is the BEST salad ever but after making it a few times I will say that you can do all these variations and it will be terrific but do NOT put the dressing into the fridge, leave it on the counter! It will not be good, it will get creamy and stay on the salad like PASTE. You can get the spinach (baby spinach is the best) and slice the strawberries with an egg slicer and toss ahead, in the fridge...but let the dressing sit on the counter, trust me. Then toss immediately before eating.

We loved this salad. I made it twice this weekend. I added candied sliced almonds... just add almond slices to a frying pan and lightly sugar the almonds, add a few drops of water to this slowly and let it cook for a few minutes.. caramelizes to a crisp, sweet. Very hot, be careful. I also added the blue cheese, mentioned by other readers. also..instead of using all that sugar, I substituted some honey for the sugar instead, which helped the dressing stick to the salad

Excellent Salad that brought rave reviews. Per others suggestions, I decreased the sugar by half. I only had red wine vinegar, so I used that. Dressing was tasty with just the right amount of sweetness for the salad. I served the dressing on the side. I added mandarin oranges, red onion and pecans!!!! Great salad!!!! Thanks Jerry.
Update: I tried the dressing with the raspberry balsamic vinegar and it was wonderful. I did increase the vinegar to a half cup and reduced the sugar in half. I think it could have used more sugar, but it was still a wonderful dressing and salad. I continue to add mandarin oranges, pecans and red onions. Great Salad!!!

I have made this for years and it is always a huge hit. For the dressing I use 1/4 cup oil, 2 T. sugar, 2 T. vinegar, 1/2 t. salt, and ground red pepper to taste. I often add mandarin oranges and fresh blueberries. Sugared almonds are a great addition as well. Great with grilled steaks and chicken. Thanks for all the great ideas for other variations!

Just made this salad for a dinner party and it was a huge hit! I will make this salad all the time now. I also halved the sugar like others recommended and substituted Raspberry Balsamic Vinegar for White Vinegar. Also, left out the seeds(I couldn't find them in the store) and used sliced almonds. Delicious.

This is an excellent salad. Instead of regular vinegar I tried Balsamic vinegar and it turned out fantastic. Also the recipe doesn't tell you to let the dressing refrigerate before serving. That is necessary to blend the flavors.

I had an abundance of strawberries from the garden this year and was looking for things to do with them. I was hesitant to make it because my husband and son are not salad people at all. However I figured "oh well more for me." Just like the other reviewers I was pleasantly surprised how much they loved it. My husband even went back for seconds! Following the advice of other reviewers, I also add red onion, crushed walnuts (pecans and almonds were also suggested) and topped it with blue cheese crumbles. Also I don't use vegetable oil so I substituted olive oil. I also couldn't find poppy seeds so I used chia seeds. It was delish! I recommend tossing in the dressing at the last minute and drizzling it on slowly for your desired coverage (I only ended up using half of it). This will definitely become a regular on our house!
I used olive oil..kept sugar at same amount as called for but added some lemon juice...no nuts
I love this recipe and have made it many times. This time, iused rice vinegar and added a strawberry. I use an immersion blender to mix. I made candied pecans in place of the seeds. Very delicious!

Excellent salad! I took this salad to Easter dinner as my contribution to the meal,and it was a big hit. The dressing was so easy to make-I used Raspberry Champagne vinegar.It gave the dressing a gorgeous red color and the sugar in the dressing really brought out the sweetness in the strawberries. I didn't used the poppy seeds, but instead used sliced almonds,which added crunch and texture.Also, I used 1/2 baby salad greens and 1/2 spinach.I've already made a 2nd batch of the dressing for my family to eat here at home, and its just great. I plan to make this again and again. Thanks for a wonderful,easy and colorful salad thats also good for you! :)

Easy to make. I used less sugar in the dressing and sliced almonds instead of the seeds. I also added mandarin oranges which added a nice color and flavor. Served this dish to friends at dinner and it was a hit!
I would halve the oil next time. I personally don't like a wet salad. I used less sugar like others recommended. The flavor was nice though. I added shredded chicken to the marinade before mixing.
Too much sesame. Just sprinkle some on instead.
Very easy to prepare. Very tasty!!! I added walnuts. It was delicious. Will definitely make it again.

My family really loved this salad. I omitted the sesame seeds, but I added mandarin orange slices and feta cheese crumbles. As has been mentioned before, I poured the dressing on just before serving, but only added half of the dressing, as that was plenty. Delicious!

I made this recipe for the first time for 65 people!!!! I multiplied all the ingredients by 8, (8 x 8=64) and used 2 giant pots to make each set of 30ish ingredients. with gloves we dished out the bowls by hand. The salad looked greasy to me; but it wasn't. At the end I sprinkled cut up pecans. It was a hit! I got several requests for the recipe and I loved the sweet sour taste. I look forward to making it for 8! Thank you for a great salad!

We love this recipe, I made it exactly as stated, the next time I decided to go all in, and I used olive oil for the oil, and added the following to the recipe, arugula, fresh minced garlic mandarin oranges, grapefruit slices, blueberries, raspberries, blackberries, pine nuts, walnut's, pecans, fresh shrimp. It was amazing! I also made a triple batch of the dressing to use for more salads the rest of the week. I’m in love with this dressing! I don’t mind the sugar as a matter of fact I loved the sweetness. I’m going to try raw sugar next time
Very tasty dish! Like others, I halved the sugar. Eat the whole thing while fresh because anything leftover will be very wilted.
